column1: # EPI_CATALOG_V1: generated by alarm_profile.py catalog from episode_blocks.py docstrings; METRICS_V1 columns + meaning, unit, level, block

column6: meaning
the coin's normal 15 min move: the median absolute 15 min move over the 24 h ending 1 h before the alarm
how far the price moved in the push direction from the run start (where the move really started) to the alarm
run_pct in the coin's normal 15 min moves
minutes from the run start to the alarm
1 = no turn (a fall of 3 normal moves) and no pause between 24 h before the alarm and the run end, so the move may be older than its start
the part of the run before the liquidations began: from the run start to the burst start, push direction (negative when the move started inside the burst)
the part since the liquidations began: from the burst start to the alarm, push direction
burst_move_pct over run_pct (when run_pct > 0): the share of the move made since the liquidations began; above 1 when the move started inside the burst
how far the price came back from the run's extreme (the furthest 3 s close in the push direction since the run start) by the alarm
giveback_pct over the move from the run start to that extreme
seconds from the burst start (the first liquidation of the burst) to the alarm
seconds from the A01 onset to the alarm
burst_move_pct per minute of the burst (NaN under 60 s)
pre_move_pct per minute from the run start to the burst start (NaN under 60 s)
burst_speed_pct_min over pre_speed_pct_min (when the move before was in the push direction): how many times faster the price moved once the liquidations began
burst_speed_pct_min over the coin's normal pace (its normal 15 min move per 15 min): 1 = the usual pace
the biggest 60 s move in the push direction inside the burst (60 s windows ending on the alarm's 5 s grid)
log10 of the forced side's liquidation USD from the burst start to the alarm (Binance publishes one print per coin per second: at least this much)
log10 of the biggest 15 s forced sum from the onset to the alarm
log10 of the biggest 60 s forced sum from the onset to the alarm
the biggest 60 s forced sum over the coin's A01 bar at the onset (its 6 h p99.9 of 60 s sums, at least 20,000 USD)
the burst's forced USD over the coin's normal day: the median forced-side USD of the 7 whole UTC days before the burst's day (days with >= 90 pct of rows known, at least 5)
the biggest 60 s forced sum over the 60 s sum at the onset: how much the burst grew after it was first seen
log10 of the forced side's liquidation USD in the hour before the burst start
seconds from the burst start to the end of the biggest 15 s of forced liquidations (the latest on ties)
seconds from the end of the biggest 15 s to the alarm

BIG waves of forced liquidations from the onset row to the alarm row: a wave starts at a 15 s sum at or above half the biggest; a new wave needs 3 consecutive known 15 s sums at or under 10 pct of the biggest since the last (an unknown sum or one in between resets that count)
share of the burst's 5 s rows holding a forced print
the biggest single 5 s row's share of the burst's forced USD (1 = one row made it all)
log10 of the OTHER side's liquidation USD over the burst (from the burst start to the alarm)
the other side's USD over both sides' USD over the burst

Binance open interest (in coins) at the last minute end at or before the alarm over the one at the last minute end at or before the burst start, minus 1 (- = positions closed; NaN when both are the same minute end or the later one is carried from an older row)
